translation_notes: EXCLUDED: the region needs the third-party `odml` package (odml.Document, odml.Section, odml.tools.RDFWriter) to build the graph it queries -- the RDFS-subclass entailment under test (a Section typed "cell" also becoming rdf:type odml:Cell, and via owlrl's DeductiveClosure rdf:type odml:Section) is produced by really running odml's RDF writer and owlrl's reasoner, not something a fixture or a shim could stand in for without inventing the very logic the test exists to check (`N'inventez pas de logique`). `odml` is not installed in ~/.venvs/ldpy (`import odml` fails with ModuleNotFoundError; `owlrl` is already there) -- `rdfeval check` fails at that import, before either side's translation is ever exercised, confirmed by driver.py's traceback. The translation below is otherwise believed correct and would be checked if the dependency were available.

this instance of `bind_initbindings` is actually `initNs=`, not `initBindings=`: NAMESPACE_MAP = {"odml": Namespace(ODML_NS), "rdf": RDF, "rdfs": RDFS} binds three PREFIXES, no variable value at all -- so the translation needs no interpolation, only @prefix odml:/rdf:/rdfs: at file scope (the query's prologue, querying.md). ODML_NS's value (https://g-node.org/odml-rdf#) is restored from odml.tools.rdf_converter.ODML_NS = Format.namespace(), read from the installed odml wheel's source since neither the region nor the file's visible imports spell it out.

each `q_string`/`curr_query = prepareQuery(...)` pair is reused for two separate `use_graph.query(curr_query)` calls (a len() check, then a for-loop) -- and `s{ }`'s value is exactly this: a reusable prepared query that re-executes on each read, so `q = s{ SELECT * WHERE {...} }` assigned once and read twice (`len(list(q))` then `for row in q`) matches the original one-for-one, including the fresh re-query on the second read.

len(list(q)), not len(q): rdflib's Result defines __len__, but ldpy's s{ } value (a PreparedQuery) does not -- `len()` on it raises TypeError (checked empirically). Materialising with list() first is the same computation rdflib's own len(Result) performs internally, so no behaviour changes. `assert not use_graph.query(curr_query)` -> `assert not q` needs no such wrapping: bool(s{ }) already executes the query and is False on zero solutions (checked empirically, for a SELECT as well as the ASK the docs show).

`@graph use_graph` is re-declared after each of the three `use_graph = rdf_writer.graph` reassignments in the function body (one per doc rebuild). Checked empirically: `@graph name` designates the graph OBJECT the name refers to at that line, not the name itself -- reassigning the Python variable afterwards does not change what later islands read without a fresh `@graph` line.

the region is a pytest test that only ever asserts and returns nothing (no mutated argument, no stdout): both files carry an identical `demo()` harness at the end (excluded from surface metrics) that turns a failed assertion into a comparable value, the same convention used for LA3D trav_existence's test_shape_declares_frame -- without it run_pair has nothing observable to compare even on a correct translation.
